headline: US must first honor Islamabad MOU commitments
dek: Araghchi: 'The American side must accept our conditions to open the strait to ships and vessels. Before such an understanding or agreement is reached, the strait will naturally be closed.' The 7-day initiative would fully reopen the waterway on the sixth day; Washington agreed to the conditions…
sources: Abbas Araghchi, Iranian FM, interview with Iraq's Al Ekhbariya TV (relayed by IRIB); reported by Gulf News, Al Jazeera liveblog, Ada Derana, Republic World
fault_line: Is the strait actually closed? Iran's conditions-on-the-table framing collides with audience 'fake news' fatigue and disputes over what's really moving — the engagement question is who can verify the ships.

sections.what_happened: Araghchi: 'The American side must accept our conditions to open the strait to ships and vessels. Before such an understanding or agreement is reached, the strait will naturally be closed.' The 7-day initiative would fully reopen the waterway on the sixth day; Washington agreed to the conditions but wanted additional provisions; Tehran will not discuss other issues until the US adheres to all commitments in the Islamabad MOU. He also said indirect talks continue through Pakistan and Qatar, and denied Iranian involvement in Red Sea developments.
sections.what_verified: Four outlets carry the same interview quotes (Gulf News, Al Jazeera liveblog, Ada Derana, Republic World/ANI). Consistent with the recorded 7-day plan (Glenn Beck/Trump4President clips circulating Oct 18-19). The 'day 6 reopen / day 7 negotiations' sequence matches Persian-language summaries circulating Oct 18-20.
sections.what_disputed: Whether Washington 'agreed to the conditions' is Araghchi's characterization only — no US confirmation in-window. Rubio (see item 02) says a deal is 'extremely difficult', cutting the other way. Social commenters dispute the premise that the strait is closed at all ('recycled rhetoric', 'fake news') — unverified audience claims, but the 138-redirected-vessels figure needs a ship-tracking (Kpler/LSEG) anchor before any Short uses it.
sections.why_matters: The paper trail of Iran's offer: day-1-to-day-6 laid out as a dated diagram (proposal date, MOU reference, day-6 reopen, day-7 negotiations) with the named source on every beat — from Tehran's framing, with Rubio's 'extremely difficult' as the stated counterpoint.
sections.context: Background: Hormuz — NEW (Oct 20 evening): Araghchi (Al Ekhbariya interview): strait stays closed until US accepts Tehran's conditions; 7-day initiative reopens it on day 6; says Washington agreed to conditions but wants additional provisions; US must first honor Islamabad MOU commitments
